title: Italian local Eucharistic book witnesses: Aquileia, Aosta, Benevento and Messina, with Padua, Monza and Ravenna gaps

traditions.label: Aquileian local Mass books
traditions.scope: The Aquileian church missal printings; individual edition identities, not a continuous normalized text.
traditions.coverage_note: Original leaves of four printings and their relations remain incompletely collated.

traditions.label: Aosta diocesan Mass books
traditions.scope: Local Missale Augustense printings for Aosta, distinct from Augsburg.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1617 book is indexed with a bishop’s decree and Ordinary; the decree and comparison with 1733 remain uninspected.

traditions.label: Benevento missal manuscripts
traditions.scope: Two separately shelfmarked Benevento missals, with scribal style and present or former holding distinguished from local liturgical authority.
traditions.coverage_note: Dates and holdings are bounded; no full recension, use history or manuscript collation is proved.

traditions.label: Messina local Missal printings
traditions.scope: Edition-identified Missale Messanense books in the examined catalogue.
traditions.coverage_note: Only the identified copies and the 1499 contents are mapped; no print-to-print revisions or adoption dates are established.

traditions.label: Padua Mass-book leads
traditions.scope: Padua-origin and Padua-held books requiring specific Mass text and use attribution.
traditions.coverage_note: No candidate in the existing Western coverage row identifies a Padua local Mass recension.

traditions.label: Monza Mass-book leads
traditions.scope: Monza-related sacramentary, chant and order-book records requiring provenance and Mass-use tests.
traditions.coverage_note: A bounded local annual ceremonial order is admitted from H14, with a documented 1101–1300 attestation in monza-local-next.json; its ff. 47–74 do not supply a complete Missal or Ordinary. F.1/101 and Berengar treasury 98/89 remain separately identified holdings without established Monza liturgical use. Full original texts, reception and sequence remain open.

traditions.label: Ravenna Mass-book leads
traditions.scope: Ravenna-attributed components and fragments requiring physical identification and use context.
traditions.coverage_note: No complete Ravenna Missal or independently dated local recension is identified in the reviewed set.

sources.title: Missale Aquileiense 1494 facsimile, dLib/Internet Archive
sources.inspection: Original facsimile images 4–5 inspected: Aquileian church caption and prefatory text concerning its liturgical custom; source review records images 525–529. Year supplied by catalogue, not those pages.
sources.limitations: Named original leaves do not establish date, full contents, act of approval, use throughout the patriarchate or difference from later prints.

sources.title: Usuarium Aquileia origin 393
sources.inspection: Books rows 164, 6908–6910 inspected: 1494, 1508, 1517 and 1519 Missale Aquileiense entries.
sources.limitations: Origin table identifies bibliographic rows; it does not collate their texts or prove succession.

sources.title: Usuarium 6909, Missale Aquileiense (1508)
sources.inspection: Original-title, 1508 date and Braidense Gerli 201 / AB.XVIII.26 holding checked against the exact book card; existing Braidense CNCE002269 record independently identifies the Venetian edition.
sources.limitations: Catalogue book identity and holding, not direct original-page reading or evidence of a new recension.

sources.title: Usuarium 164, Missale Aquileiense (1517)
sources.inspection: Original-title, age, BSB Res/4 Liturg. 393, contents rows for calendar p.40, temporal p.58, ordinary p.219, Canon p.264, sanctoral p.316, common p.384, and transcribed colophon p.452 checked.
sources.limitations: Catalogue transcription and contents index; original page images and exact predecessor comparisons are not claimed here.

sources.title: LILLIT/ICCU CNCE002271, Missale Aquileiense (1519)
sources.inspection: Bibliographic record title and imprint lines checked: Gregorio de Gregori, Venice, 15 September 1519, [12]+308 leaves; linked Gorizia copy lacks title leaf.
sources.limitations: Exact edition is identified bibliographically; Gorizia digital delivery did not yield inspected original book pages.

sources.title: Usuarium 5764, Missale Augustense (1617)
sources.inspection: Original-title, Turin printers, Arsenal FOL-Z-1397 and contents rows checked: indexed decree p.7, calendar p.13, ordinary p.206, Canon p.239, sanctoral p.315.
sources.limitations: Contents index does not read the bishop’s decree, prove its legal effect, or establish a full Roman substitution.

sources.title: Usuarium 6920, Missale Augustense (1733)
sources.inspection: Original-title, Aosta origin, 1733 date and Arsenal FOL-Z-1399 holding checked.
sources.limitations: Book body, original authority and relation to 1617 not inspected.

sources.title: Usuarium 938, Missale notatum Beneventanum VI.33
sources.inspection: Shelfmark Bibl. Cap. Benevento Cod. VI.33, approximate date, modern 1983 edition, and indexed temporal fol.1r, Canon scan p.61, Holy Week and sanctoral rows checked.
sources.limitations: Modern 1983 edition is not a second historical witness; catalogue date and component index do not prove first local use or a complete original text.

sources.title: UK Department for Culture, Beneventan Missal restitution announcement
sources.inspection: Announcement paragraphs identifying twelfth-century Missal, Benevento VI 29 = formerly Egerton 3511, and Chapter custodianship checked.
sources.limitations: Custody and Beneventan script do not prove local liturgical use, a uniform Old Beneventan rite, or exact manuscript contents.

sources.title: Usuarium 6287, Missale Beneventanum
sources.inspection: Missal genre, manuscript, former BL Egerton 3511 shelfmark and broad 1000–1200 catalogue date checked.
sources.limitations: Old shelfmark denotes the same object as VI 29; the card has no content index.

sources.title: Usuarium 7272, Missale Messanense (1480)
sources.inspection: Original-title, 1480 date and John Rylands Library 18620 shelfmark checked.
sources.limitations: No direct original-page reading or evidence that the advertised consuetudo Gallicorum means the ancient Gallican rite.

sources.title: Usuarium 382, Missale Messanense (1499)
sources.inspection: Original-title, 1499 Venetian printer, Catania Agatina Inc.1 and contents: temporal fol.1r, Ordinary fol.97r, Canon fol.100r, sanctoral fol.169r, common fol.235r checked.
sources.limitations: The title advertises correction and additions, but no exact changed reading or normative act is inspected.

sources.title: Usuarium 7276, Missale Messanense (1538)
sources.inspection: Original-title, 1538 date, BN Napoli S.Q.21.D21 and another Acireale copy noted in catalogue.
sources.limitations: The two holdings do not mean two editions; original text and relation to 1499 uncollated.

sources.title: Usuarium Padua origin 899
sources.inspection: Entire Books table inspected: pontificals and rituals, including twelve 1597 ritual entries; no Missal/Sacramentary/Gradual row.
sources.limitations: Bounded absence in this index only; does not prove absence of Padua Eucharistic books elsewhere.

sources.title: Usuarium Monza origin 1103
sources.inspection: Books table inspected for Eucharistic genre and exact Monza local attribution.
sources.limitations: Catalogue holdings and origin assignments do not themselves establish a Monza liturgical recension.

sources.title: Usuarium Ravenna origin 929
sources.inspection: Books table inspected for complete Missal identity; separate components and fragments remain leads.
sources.limitations: No corpus-wide absence of a Ravenna Missal is claimed from this table.

sources.title: Usuarium 6908, Missale Aquileiense (1494)
sources.inspection: Original-title, 1494 age and National and University Library Ljubljana Ti II 13349 shelfmark checked against exact book card.
sources.limitations: Year is catalogue-reported; inspected original front leaves do not display it.

stages.label: 1494 Aquileian Missal print
stages.scope: Local Missal book identity from inspected front leaves; text extent not collated.
stages.summary: The facsimile frontispiece names the Aquileian church; its date is catalogue attributed.

evidence.claim: The original front leaves name the Aquileian church and preserve a prefatory text about its local custom.

evidence.locus: original title, age and NUK Ljubljana Ti II 13349 fields
evidence.claim: The catalogue assigns the 1494 printing date and identifies a physical copy.

stages.limitations: The inspected pages do not give the year or establish a new text compared with any predecessor.
stages.reception: Local intended book identity, not documented adoption at each church.

stages.label: 1508 Aquileian Missal print
stages.scope: Edition-identified printed Missal; book text not inspected.
stages.witness_label: Missale iuxta ritum almae Aquileiensis ecclesiae, Braidense AB.18.0026
stages.summary: Braidense CNCE002269 and Usuarium identify a 1508 Venetian edition.

evidence.locus: Usuarium book 6909, original title, age and Braidense shelfmark fields
evidence.claim: The exact book card identifies the 1508 local Missal and Braidense copy.

stages.limitations: No changed prayer, rubric or adoption event is known.

stages.label: 1517 Aquileian Missal print
stages.scope: Indexed calendar, Mass cycles, Ordinary, Canon, common and rubrics of the 1517 print.
stages.summary: Usuarium identifies the 1517 print and indexes its main Mass divisions and colophon.

evidence.claim: The card identifies a local Missal printed in 1517 and its major divisions.

stages.limitations: Emendatissime in the title is not a collated revision claim.
stages.reception: Title names Aquileia; geographical extent of use not verified.

stages.label: 1519 Aquileian Missal print
stages.scope: Edition-identified Aquileian Missal printing; component readings uninspected.
stages.summary: ICCU title and imprint identify Venice 15 September 1519, with a Gorizia copy lacking its title.

evidence.locus: CNCE002271 title, imprint, physical description and copy note
evidence.claim: The record identifies a 1519 Aquileian print.

stages.limitations: No original book page obtained in this pass; no textual succession inferred.
stages.reception: No actual Gorizia or wider use established by present holding.

stages.label: 1617 Aosta Missal print
stages.scope: Indexed calendar, Ordinary, Canon and Mass propers in the local Missal.
stages.summary: The catalogue distinguishes the 1617 Aosta printing and indexes a decree and Mass components.

evidence.claim: A named Aosta Missal and its component locations are identified.

stages.limitations: Indexed decree unread; no effective date or whole-Missal substitution claimed.
stages.reception: Aosta destination appears in book title; reach and first use unknown.

stages.label: 1733 Aosta Missal print
stages.scope: Edition-identified Aosta Missal printing; text components uncollated.
stages.summary: Usuarium identifies a separate 1733 Aosta print at Arsenal.

evidence.locus: original title, age and shelfmark fields
evidence.claim: The card identifies this 1733 local Missal print.

stages.limitations: No comparison with 1617, approval or distinct recension demonstrated.

stages.label: Benevento VI.33 notated Missal
stages.scope: One manuscript with indexed Mass cycles and Canon.
stages.summary: Usuarium identifies the shelfmarked manuscript and its indexed Mass components.

evidence.locus: shelfmark, age and contents rows pp.61,71,83,197–279
evidence.claim: A single VI.33 manuscript is attested, with a catalogue preference for early eleventh-century date.

stages.limitations: Catalogue aliases 938/1299/6276 are not separate books; no complete text or rite-wide use established.
stages.reception: Benevento holding and apparent origin do not prove every local church used its text.

stages.label: Benevento VI.29 Missal
stages.scope: One twelfth-century Missal manuscript, formerly BL Egerton 3511; contents uncollated.
stages.summary: Government custody account and catalogue resolve two shelfmarks to one manuscript.

evidence.locus: announcement paragraphs identifying century, missal genre and two shelfmarks
evidence.claim: The report identifies the same twelfth-century manuscript under VI.29 and Egerton 3511.

stages.limitations: Provenance and Beneventan script do not establish historical liturgical use or old-rite identity.
stages.reception: Chapter custody is established; medieval local use remains unproved.

stages.label: 1480 Messina Missal print
stages.scope: Edition-identified local Missal print; original body uninspected.
stages.summary: Usuarium identifies an exact Manchester holding with a Messina title and 1480 date.

evidence.claim: A specific 1480 Messina Missal copy is identified.

stages.limitations: No original page or first-use evidence; Gallicorum is title language, not ancient Gallican rite identification.
stages.reception: Book title names Messina; church-level reception unknown.

stages.label: 1499 Messina Missal print
stages.scope: Indexed temporal, sanctoral, common, ordinary, Canon and rubrics.
stages.summary: A 1499 Venetian print for Messina is identified with an indexed Mass-book structure.

evidence.claim: The title identifies the local book and advertises sanctoral/common correction.

stages.limitations: Advertising does not verify a predecessor or exact changed reading.
stages.reception: No adoption by all Messina churches proved.

stages.label: 1538 Messina Missal print
stages.scope: Edition-identified local Missal print; text not collated.
stages.witness_label: Missale Gallicanum et Messanensis Ecclesie, BN Napoli S.Q.21.D21
stages.summary: Usuarium identifies the 1538 print and a Naples copy, with a second copy at Acireale.

evidence.locus: original title, age, Naples shelfmark and Acireale copy remark
evidence.claim: A specific 1538 Messina Missal edition is catalogued.

stages.limitations: Two holdings do not establish two states; no comparison with 1499 or normative act inspected.
stages.reception: Present Naples and Acireale holdings do not prove historical use there.

gaps.missing: Original text and authority of the four identified printings, earlier manuscript relation, and actual local reception.
gaps.next_source: Collate 1494, Braidense 1508, BSB 1517 and Gorizia 1519 original leaves, prefaces, calendars, Ordinary and propers.
gaps.consequence: Four publication events cannot be counted as three liturgical revisions or a use duration.

gaps.missing: 1617 bishop decree text, exact Ordinary readings, prior Aosta book, 1733 comparison and use.
gaps.next_source: Read Arsenal FOL-Z-1397 decree and Ordinary, compare FOL-Z-1399 and Aosta manuscript witnesses.
gaps.consequence: No reform, succession edge or effective date follows from the two printed years.

gaps.missing: Physical dating, component readings and liturgical provenance of VI.33 and VI.29.
gaps.next_source: Inspect original manuscripts or full facsimiles, colophons, calendar, Canon and additions; separate script from use.
gaps.consequence: The two shelfmarks and their custody do not define one Beneventan recension.

gaps.missing: Original pages for 1480, 1499, 1538; exact identification and copies for catalogued 1510, 1527, 1534, 1568; approval and reception.
gaps.next_source: Read Rylands 18620, Agatina Inc.1, Napoli S.Q.21.D21 and trace USTC 819816 plus other catalogue leads.
gaps.consequence: No print sequence, correction event, or ancient Gallican ancestry is established.

gaps.missing: E.57's full original Eucharistic rubrics and later layers, D.30's disputed copying date and local use, and complete earlier/later local Mass books remain uncollated; the bounded source-described E.57 and D.30 states are now owned by padua-local-round3.
gaps.next_source: See padua-local-round3 source loci and gaps; inspect E.57 ff. 89v–95r, edited sections 127g/140e and D.30 calendar/colophon. Keep D.47 Gregorian transmission separate, B.31 Roman-Franciscan and Paris Cholet volumes separate from local Padua recension.
gaps.consequence: Identified local rubrics do not certify a complete Padua Missal; custody or Pataviense labeling cannot prove a local recension.

gaps.missing: H14 local order is identified and partially edited, but original leaf collation, exact links to F.1/101 and treasury 98/89, complete Mass-text reconstruction and later reception remain unresolved.
gaps.next_source: Collate H14 ff. 47–74 and Dell’Oro–Mambretti (2001), volume A critical text pp. 431–541; identify all Mass-book cross-references and layers. Separate F.1/101 chant, sacramentary, Ambrosian formularies and lectionary; resolve its constituent dating. Resolve Berengar treasury 98/89, 846–855 versus the 860s, before 867, and Monza holding versus northeastern-French manufacture. Inspect original 1578 instruments and f-05/109, f-12/108 leaves before any local reception or substantive transition.
gaps.consequence: The local-order stage does not turn Monza-held Ambrosian/Roman sacramentaries or two late missals into a continuous local recension.

gaps.missing: Exact physical fragment identities are now bounded in ravenna-fragments, but Ravenna copying-place and church-use evidence, complete Mass/Canon extent and later reception remain unproved. Archive 011 remains an origin-unassigned, holding-only missal-calendar; the Rotulus is Advent prayer evidence with Office-use interpretation.
gaps.next_source: Collate the exact sacramentary undertexts and surviving strips against their named critical editions; obtain archive 011 calendar, colophon, Ordinary/Canon and use notes, and establish each witness's provenance and actual local reception. Keep the Rotulus recto prayers separate from later verso letters and from an annual Mass-book claim.
gaps.consequence: The three fragment attestations and present Ravenna holdings do not establish a local recension, continuous Mass-book history, complete Eucharistic prayer or normative adoption.
